name: Hydralazine
executiveSummary: Arterial vasodilator. Adult IV **5–10 mg** every 20–30 min. Pediatrics PO initial **0.25 mg/kg/dose**. Neonates IV **0.1–0.5 mg/kg/dose** every 6–8 h — cardiology.
indications:
## Indications

- Hypertension (incl. selected crises); post–cardiac surgery in pediatrics/NICU.

## Precautions

- Reflex tachycardia, hypotension. Adjust in CKD.

> Slow IV with monitoring.

adulto.dose: 5–10 mg IV every 20–30 min; max 20 mg/dose obstetric.

pediatrico.dose: Infants and children: initial 0.25 mg/kg/dose 3–4 times daily, max 25 mg/dose; increase over 3–4 weeks up to infants 5 mg/kg/day and children 7.5 mg/kg/day, max 200 mg/day. Mild–moderate renal impairment: every 8 h; severe renal impairment for rapid acetylators every 8–16 h and slow acetylators every 12–24 h. Adults: initial 10 mg every 6 h, increase 10–25 mg/dose every 2–5 days up to 300 mg/day. Usual hypertension range: 25–100 mg/day in 2 doses.
pediatrico.notes: Prolonged hydralazine use may cause pyridoxine deficiency. Indomethacin may reduce hypotensive effects. Use caution in severe renal impairment. Give with food.

neonatal.dose: **0.1–0.5 mg/kg/dose IV** slow every **6–8 h**; titrate to BP — cardiology/neonatology.

adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Palpitations, tachycardia, edema, orthostatic hypotension, headache, fever, anorexia, nausea, vomiting.
